# Guideline 0 - The spirit of Vestige Sector Vestige is a high roleplay server. The rules are the foundation: what every player must do. The Vestige Guidelines are the high roleplay we build on top of that foundation: a station that feels like a real place, full of people with lives, jobs and problems.
The short version: [color=#1b67a5]play the story, not the game.[/color] When you are unsure what to do, ask "what would my character do here?" before "what is the best play?".
- Use common sense. No ruleset can list every case, so think about what a sensible person in your character's position would do. - Do not hunt for loopholes. If you have to argue that something is "technically allowed", you have probably missed the point. - Think about how your actions affect the round and the people around you, not just yourself.
## How guidelines work Guidelines are not rules, and nobody is banned for not following one.
- If you drift away from the guidelines, an admin may remind you in game or have a quick chat with you through ahelp. That is a conversation, not a punishment. - If the same behaviour keeps coming back, it usually crosses into an actual rule, such as [textlink="escalation (R11)" link="RuleR11"], [textlink="powergaming (R16)" link="RuleM1"] or [textlink="Don't be a dick (C2)" link="RuleC2"], and it is handled under that rule. - Where a guideline and a rule seem to disagree, the rule wins.
## Context matters High roleplay lives and dies by context. The guidelines describe a normal shift, and not every shift is normal.
- Game Masters (GMs) run events, and may choose antagonists or set up situations where a guideline applies differently, or not at all. An event antagonist might be meant to open loudly, or an event might pick up a story from a previous shift. - Orders, warrants, alert levels and what is happening around your character all change what is reasonable. The same action can be fine in one situation and out of place in another. - When a GM or admin gives you direction for an event, follow it. When you are not sure how a guideline applies, ask through ahelp.
